items.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: But there was a guy named Lou Parenti, he owned a joint on Pacific Avenue... He said, “They’re gonna play here.” And we played there.

ctx.x: Wow. Interesting. The North Beach area, was there some kind of problem later on with white bands trying to take the work in that district?

Well I’ll tell you in the real early years, there’s a book here of mine with pictures in it I guess, in 1937 I think. Well in other words, in the early years they had two unions. And at one time a black musician couldn’t play east of Van Ness Avenue. You understand? Van Ness Avenue. But I played — it wasn’t my band — I was playing with another band and he had a job that played in North Beach. This was in, oh the real early thirties. It wasn’t my band, but I played.
